elements.name: Barbarian (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d12. Primary ability: Strength.

g.d: (a) Greataxe, 4 Handaxes, Explorer's Pack, and 15 GP or (b) 75 GP

elements.name: Bard (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Charisma.

g.d: (a) Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Musical Instrument of your choice, Entertainer’s Pack, and 19 GP; or (b) 90 GP

elements.name: Cleric (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Wisdom.

g.d: (a) Chain Shirt, Shield, Mace, Holy Symbol, Priest's Pack, and 7 GP; or (b) 110 GP

elements.name: Druid (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Wisdom.

g.d: (a) Leather Armor, Shield, Sickle, Druidic Focus (Quarterstaff), Explorer's Pack, Herbalism Kit, and 9 GP; or (a) 50 GP

elements.name: Fighter (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d10. Primary ability: Strength or Dexterity.

g.d: (a) Chain Mail, Greatsword, Flail, 8 Javelins, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 4 GP; (b) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or (c) 155 GP

elements.name: Monk (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Dexterity and Wisdom.

g.d: (a) Spear, 5 Daggers, Artisan’s Tools or Musical Instrument chosen for the tool proficiency above, Explorer’s Pack, and 11 GP; or (b) 50 GP

elements.name: Paladin (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d10. Primary ability: Strength and Charisma.

g.d: (a) Chain Mail, Shield, Longsword, 6 Javelins, Holy Symbol, Priest’s Pack, and 9 GP; or (b) 150 GP

elements.name: Ranger (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d10. Primary ability: Dexterity and Wisdom.

g.d: (a) Studded Leather Armor, Scimitar, Shortsword, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Druidic Focus (sprig of mistletoe), Explorer's Pack, and 7 GP; or (b) 150 GP

elements.name: Rogue (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Dexterity.

g.d: (a) Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Shortsword, Shortbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver, Thieves’ Tools, Burglar’s Pack, and 8 GP; (b) 100 GP

elements.name: Sorcerer (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d6. Primary ability: Charisma.

g.d: (a) Spear, 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (crystal), Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 28 GP; or (b) 50 GP

elements.name: Warlock (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d8. Primary ability: Charisma.

g.d: (a) Leather Armor, Sickle, 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (orb), Book, Scholar’s Pack, and 15 GP; or (b) 100 GP

elements.name: Wizard (5.2)
elements.desc: Hit die d6. Primary ability: Intelligence.

g.d: (a) 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (Quarterstaff), Robe, Spellbook, Scholar’s Pack, and 5 GP; or (b) 55 GP

elements.name: Rage
elements.desc: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

elements.name: Unarmored Defense
elements.desc: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Ar- mor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Consti- tution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

elements.name: Danger Sense
elements.desc: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

elements.name: Reckless Attack
elements.desc: You can throw aside all concern for defense to at- tack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to at- tack recklessly.

elements.name: Primal Knowledge
elements.desc: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

elements.name: Extra Attack
elements.desc: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Fast Movement
elements.desc: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

elements.name: Feral Instinct
elements.desc: Your instincts are so honed that you have Advan- tage on Initiative rolls.

elements.name: Instinctive Pounce
elements.desc: As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

elements.name: Brutal Strike
elements.desc: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Ad- vantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have Disadvantage.

elements.name: Relentless Rage
elements.desc: Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw.

elements.name: Improved Brutal Strike
elements.desc: You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

elements.name: Persistent Rage
elements.desc: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all ex- pended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

elements.name: Indomitable Might
elements.desc: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

elements.name: Primal Champion
elements.desc: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Con- stitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

elements.name: Bardic Inspiration
elements.desc: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is repre- sented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Jack of All Trades
elements.desc: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.

elements.name: Font of Inspiration
elements.desc: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic In- spiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

elements.name: Countercharm
elements.desc: You can use musical notes or words of power to dis- rupt mind-influencing effects.

elements.name: Magical Secrets
elements.desc: You've learned secrets from various magical tradi- tions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells...

elements.name: Superior Inspiration
elements.desc: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

elements.name: Words of Creation
elements.desc: You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared.

elements.name: Divine Order
elements.desc: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Channel Divinity
elements.desc: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below.

elements.name: Sear Undead
elements.desc: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together.

elements.name: Blessed Strikes
elements.desc: Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

elements.name: Divine Intervention
elements.desc: You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a

elements.name: Improved Blessed Strikes
elements.desc: The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful.

elements.name: Greater Divine Intervention
elements.desc: You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell.

elements.name: Druidic
elements.desc: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared.

elements.name: Primal Order
elements.desc: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Wild Shape
elements.desc: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below).

elements.name: Wild Companion
elements.desc: You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components.

elements.name: Wild Resurgence
elements.desc: Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required).

elements.name: Elemental Fury
elements.desc: The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

elements.name: Improved Elemental Fury
elements.desc: The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful, as detailed below.

elements.name: Beast Spells
elements.desc: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

elements.name: Archdruid
elements.desc: The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits.

elements.name: Second Wind
elements.desc: You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

elements.name: Action Surge
elements.desc: You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action.

elements.name: Tactical Mind
elements.desc: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success.

elements.name: Extra Attack
elements.desc: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Tactical Shift
elements.desc: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

elements.name: Indomitable
elements.desc: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

elements.name: Tactical Master
elements.desc: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

elements.name: Two Extra Attacks
elements.desc: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Studied Attacks
elements.desc: You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

elements.name: Three Extra Attacks
elements.desc: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Martial Arts
elements.desc: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your Unarmed Strike and Monk weapons, which are the following:

elements.name: Unarmored Defense
elements.desc: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

elements.name: Monk's Focus
elements.desc: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points.

elements.name: Unarmored Movement
elements.desc: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the Monk Features table.

elements.name: Uncanny Metabolism
elements.desc: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.

elements.name: Deflect Attacks
elements.desc: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack's total damage against you.

elements.name: Slow Fall
elements.desc: You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

elements.name: Extra Attack
elements.desc: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Stunning Strike
elements.desc: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.

elements.name: Empowered Strikes
elements.desc: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

elements.name: Evasion
elements.desc: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.

elements.name: Acrobatic Movement
elements.desc: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

elements.name: Heightened Focus
elements.desc: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits.

elements.name: Self-Restoration
elements.desc: Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the

elements.name: Deflect Energy
elements.desc: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

elements.name: Disciplined Survivor
elements.desc: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.

elements.name: Perfect Focus
elements.desc: When you roll Initiative and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

elements.name: Superior Defense
elements.desc: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

elements.name: Body and Mind
elements.desc: You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

elements.name: Lay On Hands
elements.desc: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Paladin's Smite
elements.desc: You always have the Divine Smite spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

elements.name: Channel Divinity
elements.desc: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below.

elements.name: Extra Attack
elements.desc: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Faithful Steed
elements.desc: You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the Find Steed spell prepared.

elements.name: Aura of Protection
elements.desc: You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot Emanation that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition.

elements.name: Abjure Foes
elements.desc: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe.

elements.name: Aura of Courage
elements.desc: You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

elements.name: Radiant Strikes
elements.desc: Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

elements.name: Restoring Touch
elements.desc: When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned.

elements.name: Aura Expansion
elements.desc: Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot Emanation.

elements.name: Favored Enemy
elements.desc: You always have the Hunter's Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a Long Rest.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Deft Explorer
elements.desc: Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits.

elements.name: Extra Attack
elements.desc: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

elements.name: Roving
elements.desc: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

elements.name: Tireless
elements.desc: Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits.

elements.name: Relentless Hunter
elements.desc: Taking damage can't break your Concentration on Hunter's Mark.

elements.name: Nature's Veil
elements.desc: You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn.

elements.name: Precise Hunter
elements.desc: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

elements.name: Feral Senses
elements.desc: Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

elements.name: Foe Slayer
elements.desc: The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.

elements.name: Sneak Attack
elements.desc: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a...

elements.name: Thieves' Cant
elements.desc: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in "Character Creation."

elements.name: Cunning Action
elements.desc: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

elements.name: Steady Aim
elements.desc: As a Bonus Action, you give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn.

elements.name: Cunning Strike
elements.desc: You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects.

elements.name: Uncanny Dodge
elements.desc: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

elements.name: Evasion
elements.desc: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers.

elements.name: Reliable Talent
elements.desc: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

elements.name: Improved Cunning Strike
elements.desc: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

elements.name: Devious Strikes
elements.desc: You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

elements.name: Slippery Mind
elements.desc: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control.

elements.name: Elusive
elements.desc: You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have Advantage against you unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

elements.name: Stroke of Luck
elements.desc: You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a D20 Test, you can turn the roll into a 20.

elements.name: Innate Sorcery
elements.desc: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Font of Magic
elements.desc: You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

elements.name: Metamagic
elements.desc: Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "Metamagic Options" later in this class’s description.

elements.name: Sorcerous Restoration
elements.desc: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

elements.name: Sorcery Incarnate
elements.desc: If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to activate it.

elements.name: Arcane Apotheosis
elements.desc: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

elements.name: Pact Magic
elements.desc: Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers.

elements.name: Eldritch Invocations
elements.desc: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome.

elements.name: Magical Cunning
elements.desc: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up).

elements.name: Contact Patron
elements.desc: In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the Contact Other Plane spell prepared.

elements.name: Mystic Arcanum
elements.desc: Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.

elements.name: Eldritch Master
elements.desc: When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

elements.name: Arcane Recovery
elements.desc: You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover.

elements.name: Ritual Adept
elements.desc: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn’t have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

elements.name: Spellcasting
elements.desc: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting.

elements.name: Memorize Spell
elements.desc: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

elements.name: Spell Mastery
elements.desc: You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action.

elements.name: Signature Spells
elements.desc: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot.

elements.name: Frenzy
elements.desc: If you use Reckless Attack while your Rage is active, you deal extra damage to the first target you hit on your turn with a Strength-based attack.

elements.id: Class Feature:Mindless Rage (Path of the Berserker) (5.2)
elements.name: Mindless Rage
elements.desc: You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions while your Rage is active. If you're Charmed or Frightened when you enter your Rage, the condition ends on you.

elements.name: Retaliation
elements.desc: When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

elements.id: Class Feature:Intimidating Presence (Path of the Berserker) (5.2)
elements.name: Intimidating Presence
elements.desc: As a Bonus Action, you can strike terror into others with your menacing presence and primal power.

elements.name: Bonus Proficiencies
elements.desc: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

elements.name: Cutting Words
elements.desc: You learn to use your wit to supernaturally distract, confuse, and otherwise sap the confidence and competence of others.

elements.name: Magical Discoveries
elements.desc: You learn two spells of your choice. These spells can come from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list or any combination thereof (see a class's section for its spell list).

elements.name: Peerless Skill
elements.desc: When you make an ability check or attack roll and fail, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration; roll the Bardic Inspiration die, and add the number rolled to the d20, potentially turning a failure into a success.

elements.name: Disciple of Life
elements.desc: When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores Hit Points to a creature, that creature regains additional Hit Points on the turn you cast the spell. The additional Hit Points equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

elements.name: Life Domain Spells
elements.desc: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Life Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

elements.name: Preserve Life
elements.desc: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of Hit Points equal to five times your Cleric level.

elements.name: Blessed Healer
elements.desc: The healing spells you cast on others heal you as well. Immediately after you cast a spell with a spell slot that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures other than yourself, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 plus the spell...

elements.name: Supreme Healing
elements.desc: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore Hit Points to a creature with a spell or Channel Divinity, don't roll those dice for the healing; instead use the highest number possible for each die.

elements.id: Class Feature:Circle of the Land Spells (Circle of the Land) (5.2)
elements.name: Circle of the Land Spells
elements.desc: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, choose one type of land: arid, polar, temperate, or tropical. You have the matching circle spells prepared for your Druid level and lower.

elements.id: Class Feature:Land's Aid (Circle of the Land) (5.2)
elements.name: Land's Aid
elements.desc: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Vitality-giving flowers and life-draining thorns appear for a moment in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point.

elements.id: Class Feature:Natural Recovery (Circle of the Land) (5.2)
elements.name: Natural Recovery
elements.desc: You can cast one of the level 1+ spells that you have prepared from your Circle Spells feature without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you do so again.

elements.id: Class Feature:Nature's Ward (Circle of the Land) (5.2)
elements.name: Nature's Ward
elements.desc: You are immune to the Poisoned condition, and you have Resistance to a damage type associated with your current land choice in the Circle Spells feature, as shown in the Nature's Ward table.

elements.id: Class Feature:Nature's Sanctuary (Circle of the Land) (5.2)
elements.name: Nature's Sanctuary
elements.desc: As a Magic action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape and cause spectral trees and vines to appear in a 15-foot Cube on the ground within 120 feet of yourself.

elements.name: Improved Critical
elements.desc: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

elements.name: Remarkable Athlete
elements.desc: Thanks to your athleticism, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks.

elements.name: Additional Fighting Style
elements.desc: You gain another Fighting Style feat of your choice.

elements.name: Heroic Warrior
elements.desc: The thrill of battle drives you toward victory. During combat, you can give yourself Heroic Inspiration whenever you start your turn without it.

elements.name: Superior Critical
elements.desc: Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can now score a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20 on the d20.

elements.name: Survivor
elements.desc: You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle, giving you these benefits.

elements.id: Class Feature:Open Hand Technique (Warrior of the Open Hand) (5.2)
elements.name: Open Hand Technique
elements.desc:
Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target:
- Addle. The target can't make Opportunity Attacks until the start of its next turn.
- Push. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your Focus DC or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you.
- Topple. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Focus DC or have the Prone condition.

elements.id: Class Feature:Wholeness of Body (Warrior of the Open Hand) (5.2)
elements.name: Wholeness of Body
elements.desc: You gain the ability to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled

elements.id: Class Feature:Fleet Step (Warrior of the Open Hand) (5.2)
elements.name: Fleet Step
elements.desc: When you take a Bonus Action other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that Bonus Action.

elements.id: Class Feature:Quivering Palm (Warrior of the Open Hand) (5.2)
elements.name: Quivering Palm
elements.desc: You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 4 Focus Points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last

elements.id: Class Feature:Oath of Devotion Spells (Oath of Devotion) (5.2)
elements.name: Oath of Devotion Spells
elements.desc: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Devotion Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

elements.name: Sacred Weapon
elements.desc: When you take the Attack action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to imbue one Melee weapon that you are holding with positive energy.

elements.id: Class Feature:Aura of Devotion (Oath of Devotion) (5.2)
elements.name: Aura of Devotion
elements.desc: You and your allies have Immunity to the Charmed condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Charmed ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

elements.id: Class Feature:Smite of Protection (Oath of Devotion) (5.2)
elements.name: Smite of Protection
elements.desc: Your magical smite now radiates protective energy. Whenever you cast Divine Smite, you and your allies have Half Cover while in your Aura of Protection.

elements.name: Holy Nimbus
elements.desc: As a Bonus Action, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with holy power, granting the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required).

elements.name: Hunter's Lore
elements.desc: You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey.

elements.name: Hunter's Prey
elements.desc: You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

elements.name: Defensive Tactics
elements.desc: You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

elements.name: Superior Hunter's Prey
elements.desc: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature marked by your Hunter's Mark, you can also deal that spell's extra damage to a different creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature.

elements.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
elements.desc: When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to give yourself Resistance to that damage and any other damage of the same type until the end of the current turn.

elements.name: Fast Hands
elements.desc: As a Bonus Action, you can do one of the following.

elements.name: Second-Story Work
elements.desc: You've trained to get into especially hard-to-reach places, granting you these benefits.

elements.name: Supreme Sneak
elements.desc: You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

elements.name: Use Magic Device
elements.desc: You've learned how to maximize use of magic items, granting you the following benefits.

elements.name: Thief's Reflexes
elements.desc: You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal Initiative and your second turn at your Initiative minus 10.

elements.name: Draconic Resilience
elements.desc: The magic in your body manifests physical traits of your draconic gift. Your Hit Point maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.

elements.name: Draconic Spells
elements.desc: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

elements.name: Elemental Affinity
elements.desc: Your draconic magic has an affinity with a damage type associated with dragons. Choose one of those types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

elements.name: Dragon Wings
elements.desc: As a Bonus Action, you can cause draconic wings to appear on your back. The wings last for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration, you have a Fly Speed of 60 feet.

elements.name: Dragon Companion
elements.desc: You can cast Summon Dragon without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

elements.name: Dark One's Blessing
elements.desc: When you reduce an enemy to 0 Hit Points, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1 Temporary Hit Point).

elements.name: Fiend Spells
elements.desc: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

elements.id: Class Feature:Dark One's Own Luck (Fiend Patron) (5.2)
elements.name: Dark One's Own Luck
elements.desc: You can call on your fiendish patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add 1d10 to your roll.

elements.name: Fiendish Resilience
elements.desc: Choose one damage type, other than Force, whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest. You have Resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

elements.name: Hurl Through Hell
elements.desc: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes.

elements.name: Evocation Savant
elements.desc: Choose two Wizard spells from the Evocation school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

elements.name: Potent Cantrip
elements.desc: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target...

elements.name: Sculpt Spells
elements.desc: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level.

elements.name: Empowered Evocation
elements.desc: Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

elements.name: Overchannel
elements.desc: You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1-5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

elements.desc: Circle spells for the arid land.

elements.desc: Circle spells for the polar land.

elements.name: Temperate
elements.desc: Circle spells for the temperate land.
